accepted_findings.reason: False positive: SQL strings are built from compile-time constants (column lists, whitelisted SET fragments, static WHERE clauses). User-controlled values are always passed as psycopg %s parameters; dynamic OR/SET parts use only server-side whitelists.
False positive: OAuth2 token_type literal 'bearer' in auth responses, not a credential.
False positive: HTTP header name constant for dashboard share auth, not a secret value.
False positive: JSON field password_required (boolean), not a hardcoded password.
False positive: user-secret service key identifier string (USER_SECRET_KEY), not a PAT value.
False positive: Lucide icon name for secrets-related tools, not a password.
False positive: settings key name for SimpleSecCheck API key storage, not the key itself.
False positive: default None placeholders in operator settings row dict; keys like discord_bot_token hold no literal secret.
False positive: German placeholder examples in generated curl snippets for OTP secret registration; not real credentials.
False positive: pytest uses dummy credentials (password1, pw, x, secret-value, app-password samples) to exercise auth/secret tools; never shipped to production.
False positive: function-call test passwords in tests/test_auth_setup.py and similar; isolated test doubles only.
False positive: tempfile.TemporaryDirectory in pytest creates private per-test dirs; acceptable for unit/integration tests, not production /tmp races.

Acceptable: intentional best-effort cleanup (IMAP logout, optional reindex after git pull, search index teardown, verify-run persistence, e2e fixture teardown) where failure must not block the primary path.
Acceptable: skip malformed preset/config JSON when iterating filesystem data; errors are isolated per file.
False positive: random.randint seeds ComfyUI KSampler nodes for image generation reproducibility, not security-sensitive tokens.
Acceptable: subprocess used for LSP, fixed git -C/clone argv lists, ripgrep workspace search, coding-shell tools, and test harnesses; required product functionality.

Acceptable: subprocess uses shell=False with argv lists; git/rg use fixed executables; bash and workspace_verify use shlex.split plus coding bash blocklist and workspace path guards; tests invoke controlled git/npm fixtures.
False positive: git/rg/npm resolved via PATH is intentional; commands are fixed argv lists with no shell.
False positive: standard pytest assertions in test modules; not production -O bytecode.
False positive: discord.py on_ready invariant (self.user set after login); type-narrowing only, not security enforcement.
False positive: unreachable invariant after early error return (extra_root_or_error / path resolution); documents type narrow for mypy, not runtime security.
Accepted: no HEALTHCHECK in application image; liveness/readiness probes are configured at orchestration layer (compose/Kubernetes), not in this Dockerfile.
Accepted: application image intentionally omits USER; process identity is constrained at deploy time (compose/Kubernetes securityContext) rather than in this multi-stage build Dockerfile.
Informational: Python CodeQL queries in type stub files (.pyi) and generated code — no runtime execution path.
False Positive: Svelte/Vue use reactive bindings preventing XSS.
Acceptable: SQL injection query in test file only with mock database.
False Positive: File access restricted to known static asset directories with normalization.
Acceptable: Health check endpoints intentionally expose version/status for monitoring.
Acceptable: TypeScript declaration files .d.ts are type-only, no executable code.
Acceptable: Go security queries in test files only with controlled inputs.
False positive: workspace and tool paths resolve through workspace_resolver / tool_factory guards (owner check, root containment, deny .. and unsafe segments) before filesystem access.
False positive: API surfaces str(exception) or truncated detail for operator debugging; full tracebacks are not returned to clients (logged server-side only).
False positive: log format strings mention modules/features named secret/password/token; logged values are counts, IDs, flags, or scrubbed metadata—never raw credentials.
False positive: SHA-256 used for query activation fingerprints and share-token/password derivations with server-side pepper context—not for storing user login passwords.
False positive: regexes parse bounded agent tool-call syntax and setup validation; inputs are length-limited chat/tool payloads, not unbounded attacker-controlled megastrings.
False positive: outbound LLM base URL comes from operator-configured provider settings (trusted admin), not arbitrary end-user URL parameters.

False positive: host checks gate known provider domains (generativelanguage.googleapis.com, calendar.google.com) after URL parse; not sole defense but combined with HTTPS and operator-only configuration.
False positive: generated lore text persisted to RAG may contain narrative 'password' wording; not storage of user credentials.

False positive: dynamic Record/object indexing uses API/schema keys or numeric indices; prototype-pollution paths blocked where user paths are accepted (dashboardDataPaths guards __proto__/constructor/prototype).
False positive: RegExp built from i18n or user-facing search patterns with bounded input in UI code, not server-side RE DoS surface.
False positive: eslint-disable when react-hooks plugin is not loaded in security scan context; rule definition missing in CI eslint config, not a security defect.
Accepted risk: esbuild dev-server CORS issue affects local `vite` dev only; production ships vite build output via backend static files, not esbuild serve.

Accepted risk: PostCSS stringify XSS requires attacker-controlled CSS through an app that embeds user CSS in <style>; frontend uses compiled Tailwind build output, not user-supplied raw CSS AST round-trip.
Accepted risk: Vite dev-server .map path traversal requires --host exposure and predictable paths; production Docker image serves prebuilt dist without Vite dev server.
Accepted risk: esbuild dev-server CORS issue affects local `vite` dev only; production ships vite build output via backend static files, not esbuild serve.

Accepted risk: PostCSS stringify XSS requires attacker-controlled CSS through an app that embeds user CSS in <style>; frontend uses compiled Tailwind build output, not user-supplied raw CSS AST round-trip.
Accepted risk: Vite dev-server .map path traversal requires --host exposure and predictable paths; production Docker image serves prebuilt dist without Vite dev server.

False positive: psycopg3 cursor.execute uses %s placeholders for all values; dynamic SQL fragments are compile-time column lists (WORKSPACE_SELECT_SQL, _GRAPH_NODE_SELECT), whitelisted UPDATE SET keys (ALLOWED_UPDATE_COLUMNS, _SETTING_KEYS), fixed WHERE templates, or migration DDL with constant identifiers—never interpolated user input.
False positive: Alembic migration DDL uses f-strings only for constant table/column names defined in the same revision file, not request-time user input.
False positive: Semgrep matches a comment mentioning ws://; runtime default PIDEA_CDP_HTTP_URL is http://127.0.0.1:9222 (HTTP CDP), not an insecure WebSocket client connection.
Accepted: application image intentionally omits USER; process identity is constrained at deploy time (compose/Kubernetes securityContext) rather than in this multi-stage build Dockerfile.
Accepted: same as missing-user-entrypoint—root in build/runtime is a deliberate tradeoff for this single-service Python image; non-root USER can be added when orchestration requires it.

False positive: optional user context is passed through _sanitize_prompt_input before inclusion; scheduled lore workflow with fixed system prompt—LLM input surface is operator-controlled, not a direct SQL/command injection path.
False positive: static log message templates contain subsystem names (chat_secret_vault, provider_prompt_tokens); no secret values are interpolated into logger calls.
False positive: logs embedding model token limits and truncation sizes, not API keys or user secrets.
False positive: dev-only i18n validation scripts concatenate file paths into console.log; not exposed to untrusted format-string input at runtime.
False positive: getPath/setPath explicitly reject __proto__, constructor, and prototype segments before bracket assignment.
False positive: operator maintenance scripts build http(s) URLs from AGENT_BASE_URL env plus fixed API paths; not end-user-controlled file:// fetches.
False positive: TruffleHog hits in this repo are documentation placeholders, test fixtures, or example curl snippets—not live production credentials.
